records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
The grace period for F-1 students is **60 days** after your program ends. It also applies to your dependents. After post-completion OPT, you get another 60-day grace period once your OPT EAD card expires, but only if you completed the OPT and did not exceed the 90-day unemployment limit.

**During the grace period you may:**
- Prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the U.S.

**You may not** work or study during this time.

**What you're expected to do:** If you are not applying for OPT or extending your legal status, you should leave the U.S. within the 60 days. If you leave before the grace period ends, you can't re-enter on your F-1 status after your I-20 expiration date. If USCIS receives your OPT application before the 60 days end, your F-1 status stays active until USCIS decides.

**Proposed change:** In September 2025, DHS proposed a rule that would replace "duration of status" with fixed periods of stay and shorten the F-1 grace period from 60 to 30 days. It is only a proposal. The excerpts I have don't say it has been finalized, so the 60-day period is what ISSS currently lists. Please confirm with an ISSS advisor before relying on either number for your own plans.

records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
A J-1 master's student can do Academic Training (AT) for up to **18 months**, or the length of their degree program, whichever is shorter. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension.

Key conditions from ISSS:
- AT during your studies and AT after your program ends are added together toward this limit. Full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- AT can be paid or unpaid, part-time or full-time, and with one or more employers.
- It must be directly related to the major field of study on your DS-2019.
- It must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- To apply, submit the Academic Training form (on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx)) at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends submitting at least three weeks ahead of when you need approval, since review takes about 4-5 business days.

On the duration of status rule: DHS published a final rule that would change how long J-1 students are admitted and require a USCIS extension for post-completion AT. On September 14, 2026, a federal court postponed its effective date and barred DHS from implementing it. ISSS is monitoring this and will update its guidance.

For your specific situation, including the STEM extension, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

Sources: [Academic Training for J-1 Students](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment), [Court postponement announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status)

records.question: Is the new rule ending duration of status in effect now?
search_queries: Is the new rule ending duration of status in effect now?
records.answer:
No. The rule is not in effect right now, according to the latest ISSS announcement.

- **July 17, 2026:** DHS published a final rule eliminating "duration of status" (D/S) for F and J nonimmigrants. It was scheduled to take effect on September 15, 2026.
- **September 14, 2026 (newest update):** The U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a preliminary injunction postponing the effective date. Under the court's order, the rule did not go into effect on September 15, and DHS is barred from implementing it.

ISSS says it is closely monitoring the situation and any guidance from DHS, ICE, USCIS, and the Department of State. It will update its guidance as more information becomes available. I didn't find anything newer than the September 14 announcement, so the situation could change. Check the ISSS site for updates.

If the rule does take effect later, the July announcement says F and J students entering the U.S. would receive a date-specific I-94 for a fixed period, up to four years. Those needing more time would have to apply to USCIS for an extension of stay or travel and seek a new admission. For now, the injunction means this is not being implemented.

For questions about your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor. ISSS also has an FAQ page on the rule in the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status-(D-S)---FAQs.aspx).

Sources:
- [Court postpones effective date (Sept 14, 2026)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status)
- [DHS publishes final rule (July 17, 2026)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/July/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Publishes-Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status)

records.question: How do I apply for CPT?
search_queries: How do I apply for CPT?
records.answer:
To apply for CPT, first confirm that the training is a required part of your program, then submit your application to ISSS for final review.

**Steps**
1. **Check eligibility.** You need to have been enrolled full-time and physically present in the U.S. for at least one full academic year (3 quarters or 2 semesters). There is an exception for graduate students whose programs require immediate CPT. You also need a training offer related to your field, and the training must be required for all students in your program to graduate.
2. **Get your program's approval first.**
   - Co-op students: meet with your Steinbright Career Development Center Co-op Advisor.
   - Non-co-op students: meet with your academic advisor to confirm the CPT is required by your program's curriculum.
   - PhD students (dissertation-related work): you also need secondary approval from the Office of Graduate Studies and a written statement from your PhD advisor explaining why the off-campus training is required.
3. **Submit your CPT application to ISSS.** The forms are on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

**Keep in mind**
- You can't start work before the official CPT start date. The dates follow the Drexel academic calendar.
- Non-co-op CPT is authorized term by term.
- If a course goes with the requirement, you generally must be registered for it during the CPT term.
- CPT is generally limited to 20 hours per week, with some exceptions.
- Full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more eliminates your eligibility for OPT.

For questions about your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

Source: [CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)

records.question: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
search_queries: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
records.answer:
It depends on the type of CPT:

- **Full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more eliminates your eligibility for OPT.** The OPT page likewise says you need fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT at your current educational level, and that accumulating more than 364 days is a common reason for denial.
- **Part-time CPT or international co-op does not affect your OPT eligibility.**

Keep in mind that CPT is usually limited to 20 hours per week, except for full-time co-op programs, CPT during an approved vacation or break term, or programs that require full-time practical training. Those full-time exceptions are the ones that count toward the 364-day limit, so track your full-time CPT days carefully.

If you're planning several terms of full-time CPT or co-op, it's worth confirming your running total with an ISSS advisor, since decisions about your own status should be checked with them.

records.question: Which countries are affected by the travel ban proclamation?
search_queries: Which countries are affected by the travel ban proclamation?
records.answer:
The most recent country list on the ISSS website comes from the expanded proclamation (signed December 16, 2025, effective January 1, 2026). It covers 38 countries plus the Palestinian territories. F and J visas are suspended for both full- and partial-restriction countries.

**Countries listed in ISSS's January 2026 announcement:**
Afghanistan, Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burma, Burundi, Chad, Republic of Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Cuba, Dominica, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Gabon, The Gambia, Haiti, Iran, Laos, Libya, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Turkmenistan, Venezuela, Yemen, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. People traveling on Palestinian Authority-issued or -endorsed travel documents are also covered.

**Notes:**
- That list has 39 names, while the December announcement says 38 countries. The January page also says Turkmenistan is listed, but the December page says its partial ban was lifted. Please confirm the exact list with ISSS or the official proclamation.
- The earlier June 2025 proclamation covered 19 countries. It is now history, superseded by the December 2025 expansion.
- The ISSS excerpts don't spell out which countries are full versus partial bans under the new proclamation. For exceptions and how this applies to you, check with an ISSS advisor.

**Sources:**
- [Expansion of Presidential Proclamation (Dec 17, 2025)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/December/presidential-proclamation-expansion-restricting-entry-us)
- [USCIS policy memorandum announcement (Jan 8, 2026)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/January/USCIS-issues-a-policy-memorandum-that-places-a-hold-on-all-pending-applications-for-individuals-from)

records.question: How do I apply for it?
history: Can I work off campus during my first year if my program requires an internship?
search_queries: How do I apply for it? | Can I work off campus during my first year if my program requires an internship?
records.answer:
To apply for CPT, follow this process from the ISSS CPT page:

1. **Get your program's confirmation first.**
   - **Co-op students:** meet with your Steinbright Career Development Center Co-op Advisor to start the CPT process.
   - **Non-co-op students:** meet with your academic advisor to confirm the proposed CPT is required for your program's established curriculum.
   - **PhD students** requesting CPT for off-campus work related to their dissertation: you need secondary approval from the Office of Graduate Studies and a written statement from your PhD advisor explaining why the off-campus training is required to complete your dissertation.
2. **Submit your CPT application to ISSS** for final review. The forms are on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

**Timing and conditions:**
- CPT start and end dates follow the official term dates in the Drexel academic calendar. Don't begin any CPT work before the official CPT start date.
- Non-co-op experiential programs need CPT authorization term by term. Co-op CPT follows the established co-op cycle dates.
- Full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more eliminates your eligibility for OPT. Part-time CPT and international co-op don't affect it.

I couldn't find application deadlines or processing times in these excerpts, so please confirm them with an ISSS advisor before you plan a start date.
